endorsements.quote: Further, hospitals should require regular audits of AI performance impacts on clinical decision making and health outcomes to ensure critical variables with high predictive value are not overlooked in favor of user preferences.

unlisted_practices: Hospital governance, developers, and policymakers should establish limits on an AI tool's accommodation of user preferences, balancing trust and engagement against accuracy and comprehensiveness.
Developers should prioritize design elements that let users access ground truths in high-stakes domains.
Developers should prepare design impact statements that evaluate how curating information for engagement or acceptability might exclude important information or perpetuate biases.
Developers should adopt design choices that ensure users are made aware of domain-critical information even when it does not align with user preferences or past interactions.
Developers should document personalization parameters across use cases to build an evidence base of impacts.

Developers and policymakers should use decision science and UX experimentation such as A/B testing to identify interface designs that promote critical thinking and consideration of alternative perspectives.

Developers should integrate alternative perspectives into AI outputs and use design features such as accordion menus, pop-up windows, and progressive disclosure to increase awareness of contextual information.
Developers should use prompt strategies that provide stepwise instructions and chain-of-thought explanations to enable critical evaluation of outputs.
Developers should provide metadata or nutrition-facts-style labels on AI outputs so users can assess accuracy, reliability, and fairness.
Developers should use design approaches that decelerate heuristic thinking and mitigate automation bias and other cognitive biases.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/critique article cautioning against customized/personalized AI in healthcare and high-stakes domains due to risks of information restriction and bias.
